prisoner.name: Nicole d’Entremont
prisoner.description: Nicole d’Entremont was a Catholic Worker editor jailed after an antiwar sit-down at New York’s Armed Forces Day parade in 1966.

cases.charges: Antiwar sit-down; individual statutory charge not verified
cases.sentence: Five-day jail sentence; three additional days of pretrial custody after refusing bail. A separate contemporary report confirms her return from the five-day term. Exact custody endpoints remain unverified.

prisoner.name: Dianne Feeley
prisoner.description: Dianne Feeley participated in Catholic Worker antiwar actions before joining the Young Socialist Alliance in 1967. She later became a labor and feminist organizer.

cases.charges: Antiwar sit-down; individual statutory charge not verified
cases.sentence: Three days of pretrial custody after refusing bail; subsequently reported in jail serving a five-day sentence. Completion of that additional term and exact release date remain unverified.

prisoner.name: Patricia Rusk
prisoner.description: Patricia Rusk participated in the Assembly of Unrepresented People’s antiwar sit-down in Washington, D.C. She described her imprisonment in the Catholic Worker.

cases.charges: Antiwar sit-down; individual statutory charge not verified
cases.sentence: Served five days in D.C. Jail following the August 9, 1965 antiwar sit-down. Exact release date and individual charge wording remain unverified.

entries.custody_evidence: First-person five-day jail account describes arrest, overnight transfer and subsequent days; two other columns corroborate completed custody.
